Overseer Malvek — Faction Dossier
Asset Classification & Lore Registry  ·  Visual Reference Edition
Classification: Hostile Architecture The subject of this dossier has not been directly observed.
All entries document his assets, not his person.
His absence is the point.
— Field Command — Confirmed Fallen
Marrow Vex
Visual Reference — Confirmed Field Identity — Styx Station
Affiliate Southern Operations — Field Commander
Marrow Vex
Operational Authority: Styx Station
Furnace Proximity Classification: Extended
Status: Fallen — Episode VII

More body than armor. The armoring is partial and functional, not decorative. Nothing slows the thermal regulation his enhanced metabolism requires. Everything else is replaceable. That cannot be.

The red-tinged scarring across the skull is not cosmetic. It is the specific discoloration produced by proximity to unauthorized Furnace processing over a long operational career. He stood in the heat of other people's transformations for years. He chose to stay close. The heat remembers.

He never raised his voice because he never needed to. The people beneath him in the operation did what he said because the alternative was not survivable. He was never cruel about it. Cruelty requires emotion. He was efficient.

Arc Note: Vex falls at Styx in Episode VII. His defeat is real and earned. It changes nothing systemic. He was the face of the operation. Not the architect. When he falls, the architecture remains. Malvek recalculates. The War Golem is fitted.
— Malvek's Third Category —
Deadman Alchemists

The Forge Mystics were the network's human interpreters. Not Sirens — they never underwent transformation. They read the network through learned sensitivity: decoding Forge script, tracking Ley line fluctuations, interpreting system behavior they could perceive but not command. The network tolerated their presence because their sensitivity was genuine, if incomplete.

Malvek ran them through the Furnace. Not to resurrect them — they were alive. Not to harden them — they were not Sirens. He ran them through to extract their sensitivity, fuse it with Forge alloy, and bind the result to a chassis capable of operating in environments that would destroy an unmodified human. The Furnace was not designed for this. It processed what it was given.

The Third Category: Not Goblin — mechanical horror, manufactured, never alive. Not Witch — tragic horror, broken resurrection, memory as wound. Deadman Alchemist — voluntary horror. They agreed to the process, or were made to agree in circumstances the story has not yet revealed. Human expertise transformed into an operational tool by someone who understood exactly what he was destroying to make it.
Deadman Alchemist — Type I
Furnace Process: Irreconciled
"The Composite"
The most physically transformed. Multiple skull-face forms visible on the chassis — not separate entities, but the visual record of a process that tried to reconcile irreconcilable things and left the evidence on the surface. Function: Unauthorized Furnace operation. Can maintain access longer than any other Alchemist type. The instability that made it is the same quality that makes it impossible to shut down.
Deadman Alchemist — Type II
Furnace Process: Bifurcated
"The Duplex"
Two identities compressed into one operational unit. The original Forge Mystic persists in subordinated form beneath what the Furnace produced. The chain connecting them is not decorative — it is load-bearing. Function: Network interpretation under corruption. The internal conflict produces sensitivity to contradictory signals that clean processing cannot match.
Deadman Alchemist — Type III
Furnace Process: Externalized
"The Signal"
The most organic-seeming. The cable-tendril structures are Forge script made physical — sensitivity that was once learned is now structural. Ley line frequency runs through the cables rather than being perceived through them. Function: Long-range Forge Network interference. The lateral pull Brae felt in the corrupted transit shaft to Styx — that was The Signal running interference.
Deadman Alchemist — Type IV / Senior Proxy
Furnace Process: Clean Integration
"The Hand"
The most composed. Forge sigils grew into the alloy during the process — not inscribed afterward. The orange eye signature is Siren-adjacent. Not a Siren. Close enough to be dangerous. Function: Malvek's direct field proxy. Directs the other Alchemists. If Vex was the weapon, The Hand is the targeting system. Still operational after Styx.
Distinction: Deadman Alchemists are not Glitch Witches. Witches are Sirens broken by the Furnace. Alchemists are Forge Mystics transformed by it — different input, different output, different horror. They retain functional coherence. The horror is not brokenness. The horror is that they work.
— Styx Station — Active Extraction State —
The Corrupted Node Portal
Styx Gateway — Affiliate Extraction Operation / Active
The Portal Under Extraction
This is not what the Gateway looks like at rest. This is what it looks like when it is being used against its nature.

The Gateway's natural energy signature is Forge amber and teal — the same spectrum as the network it connects to. The green is contamination. Malvek's extraction operation has been forcing the Gateway open in the wrong direction, pulling FROM the Enigmatic Universe rather than allowing natural interface flow. The green is the Enigmatic Universe's energy bleeding back into the Forge infrastructure around the junction point.

The skull entity at the center of the arch: the Enigmatic Universe does not have faces. But when something vast is forced through an aperture it was not designed to pass through, it takes the shape of the opening. The archway has skull carvings. What comes through wears skulls.

Critical Distinction: The TRUE Gateway that Brae perceives at the end of Episode VII shows movement "like weather behind glass" — dark, patient, Forge-amber at the edges. The CORRUPTED PORTAL shown here is the Gateway during an active extraction cycle. Brae arrives just after Vex falls — extraction still running, not at full operation. Full corrupted state is Arc Two territory.
Story rule: The entity being extracted from is not hostile — yet. It is being used against its nature. What happens to something of that scale when extraction continues long enough is the question the second arc is built toward answering.
— Gateway-Contaminated Units —
Styx Station Goblins

The standard Glitch Goblin runs on Mint-to-Deploy authorization with Forge Network override capability. Its optic signature is amber. Its logic is Kaiju-ash construction running on copper nerve-lines engineered to mimic Forge Network pathways.

The Goblins stationed at Styx Station are different. Not redesigned — contaminated. Proximity to the corrupted Portal has been rewriting their copper nerve-line logic at a rate no one in the Affiliate operation tracked or reported. They have been stationed at Styx long enough that the Gateway's extraction energy has found its way into their signal architecture. Their optic color has shifted toward the Portal's green. They respond to Gateway pulses the way standard Goblins respond to Mint authorization signals.

Threat classification: These units are not operating on Affiliate authorization. They are not operating on Forge Network override. They are operating on something that comes from the other side of the Portal. What that signal is, who or what is sending it, and whether it constitutes intent is the first question Brae will need to answer when she encounters them at Styx.
Styx Goblin — Sentinel Configuration / Gateway-Contaminated
Styx Station — Long-Range Sentinel
"The Crow"
Robed configuration. Staff-equipped. Positioned at the Gateway seal itself as the outermost sentinel line. The staff is a signal amplifier — originally built to broadcast Mint authorization to subordinate Goblins across the station. After Gateway contamination, it now broadcasts something else: a frequency that has no designation in the Forge Network catalogue. It reaches Goblins three stations away. What it tells them is not yet understood.

Lore note: The robe and hood configuration is not Affiliate design. Standard Goblin chassis do not include fabric coverings. Someone — or the contamination itself — added these. The Crow configured itself.
Styx Goblin — Furnace Operations / Gateway-Contaminated
Styx Station — Unauthorized Furnace Guardian
"The Warden"
Stationed at the unauthorized Furnace processing column — the equipment the Affiliates built into Styx Station to run Siren units through without network authorization. The column beside it IS the Affiliate Furnace extension: green-lit Forge processing hardware, still running, still cycling through material even with Vex gone.

The Warden's function was Furnace guarding and operation maintenance. After Gateway contamination, it has expanded that mandate. It now maintains the Furnace operation regardless of authorization. It does not wait for a Mint Card. It does not wait for Vex. It runs the Furnace because the signal from the Portal tells it to.

Encounter implication: The Warden will be running unauthorized Furnace cycles after Vex falls. Brae arriving at Styx means arriving while the Furnace is still active. What it is processing when she gets there is not yet written.
— Tragic Horror — Coherence Through Corruption —
Siren Witch Commander
Glitch Witch — Commander Class / Gateway-Coherent
Siren Witch Commander
Origin: High-Class Siren — Furnace Failure State
Core Status: Cracked / Gateway-Synchronized
Designation: Unassigned — Classification Contested

She was a Siren of high operational class before the Furnace failure. The standard Witch failure pattern produces a unit that retains Siren capability with corrupted network connection — unpredictable, dangerous, incoherent. That is not what she is.

Her Core broke in a specific way. Rather than producing total signal incoherence, the fractures let something else in. The Enigmatic Universe's energy bleeding through the corrupted Portal found the crack in her Core and filled it. The result is a Witch who receives two signals simultaneously: the broken remnant of her Forge Network connection, and something from the other side of the Gateway that her fractured Core can hold coherently when her original signal could not.

She did not become a Commander because the Affiliates appointed her. She became a Commander because the other Witches in the Styx Station area oriented to her. A broken Core broadcasts nothing — hers broadcasts the Gateway signal. Other Witches, operating on fragments of lost network connection, turned toward her frequency the way damaged instruments turn toward the strongest available signal.

She organized them. Not through command. Through being the loudest thing they could still hear.

The blue stones in her crown and chest: These are the remnants of her original node stone Core — cracked but not destroyed. In the light of the Forge Network they read as corrupted. In the light of the Gateway they read as lenses. She sees through both simultaneously. What that composite perception shows her is the most important unanswered question about her character.
Arc potential: She is not an enemy the story can afford to treat as a standard boss encounter. She is a Siren who went wrong in a specific enough way to produce something new. Whether what she has become is a tragedy to be resolved, a threat to be ended, or an asset the network would recognize if it could perceive her correctly — that question must remain open past the first time Brae meets her.
Critical distinction from standard Witches: Standard Witches are tragic horror — memory as wound, capability without coherence. The Commander is something the existing categories do not fully cover. She has a form of coherence. It is just not the coherence she was built for. Do not write her as simply a more powerful Witch. Write her as something that needs a new category.
— Independent Faction — Neutral Classification Contested —
Steamfitter Rare Combat Automaton
Steamfitters Guild — Rare Unit / Station City Calibration Platform
Independent Guild — Automaton Engineering / Non-Affiliate
Rare Combat Automaton
Steamfitters Guild — Senior Designation
Energy Signature: Forge-Adjacent / Clean
Location: Station City Calibration Platform

The Steamfitters are an independent engineering guild predating both the Affiliates and the CST on the southern line. They build automatons using Forge Network-adjacent processes — not the full Furnace system, not Mint-to-Deploy authorization chains, not Goblin alloy. Their construction methodology is older and their relationship to the Forge Network is different: not exploitation, not ignorance, but a form of respectful adjacency developed over generations of careful study.

Their Rare Combat Automaton units are among the most capable non-Siren constructs in existence. The blue energy visible in the palms is Forge-adjacent but uncontaminated — clean signal, properly channeled. The massive circular calibration wheel behind the unit is a Steamfitter Guild sigil, a Forge Network chart they can read without being Sirens. The feathered crest identifies this as a senior Rare designation.

The background establishes this unit's location: Station City. The tower density visible behind the calibration platform is consistent with Metro Center proximity — the Steamfitters operate at the highest network density areas because that is where their work is most precise and most necessary.

Faction placement: The Steamfitters are neither Affiliate nor CST. They are independent contractors who have been working the southern line for longer than either organization has existed. Their relationship to the Forge Network is not parasitic. Their automatons carry clean Forge signal rather than corrupted or Goblin-alloy construction. They are a potential alliance, a neutral complication, or a source of knowledge about the network that predates the current crisis.
Story implication: A Rare Steamfitter unit at Station City, on a calibration platform, in the middle of the Affiliate operation in the south — this unit is there for a reason. The Steamfitters know something is wrong with the southern network. They have been tracking it from their calibration platforms at Metro Center. What they know, and whether they will share it, is the next question the story needs to answer on the road to Station City.
— Malvek's Primary Field Asset — Unequipped —
The War Golem
War Golem — Unequipped / No Furnace Shield / MTD Ports Not Visible
Malvek's Primary Mobile Asset — Southern Operations
The War Golem
Status: Unequipped — Furnace Shield Not Fitted
Height: Approximately 4 stories
Optic Classification: Forge-Frequency Vision / Fog-Penetrating

Monolithic. The city towers visible behind it establish scale — it stands above the station structure it is deployed from. The smooth front chassis is a restraint: it is the image of capability that has not yet been called upon.

The orange-ember optic clusters filter through Forge Network interference — the same fog that degrades every other unit's sensors is transparent to it. In the Stones Throw fog, or the approach fog to any southern station, the War Golem sees clearly while remaining invisible within it. It is a weapon designed for environments the Affiliates helped make hostile.

When the Furnace Shield is Fitted

  • 12 MTD Ports active on the shield face — the Golem becomes a walking Mint-to-Deploy authorization hub. Touch a Goblin to a port: deployed, network-overridden, War Golem as controller
  • Compact Furnace processing chamber in the shield cavity — field-level hardening on Goblin units mid-operation. Cannot perform resurrection. Can perform targeted damage to Siren Cores.
  • Network interference broadcasting — the equipped Golem disrupts Siren Hyperchamber perception within a radius proportional to the extraction operation's intensity
  • Combined: a mobile Affiliate operations hub. Goblin authorization, Furnace access, and interference broadcasting — walking.
Deployment signal: The War Golem unequipped means the situation is being managed. The War Golem with the Furnace Shield fitted means Malvek has decided the situation is no longer being managed. Vex falling at Styx is the event that triggers fitting. Its first equipped deployment is Arc Two's opening statement.
— The Subject of This Dossier —
Malvek's Absence
Overseer Malvek — Design Principle
The four Alchemists — made from people he understood completely enough to destroy deliberately.
The War Golem — built to the scale of a problem he anticipated before it existed.
The contaminated Goblins at Styx — not a failure of containment but evidence of how long he has been running this operation.
The Witch Commander — either an asset he is cultivating or a variable he has not yet resolved. The ambiguity is his.
The Steamfitters — the one faction the dossier cannot place in his operational architecture. That gap may be the story's most important opening.
Vex — the face. Now gone.

Malvek designed all of these. He appears in none of them.

His visual introduction — when it comes — must cost the audience something.
We have seen everything he built.
We have not seen him.
Protect that gap.
